reference_title: Design and Construction of Continuous Flight Auger Piles
chapter_title: Guide Construction Specifications for Continuous Flight Auger (CFA) Piles

sections.title: Description
sections.summary: Guide specification scope: the CFA Pile Contractor furnishes design, materials, equipment and labor and designs and installs CFA piles (type, diameter, length, cap connection, means and methods) for the plan load capacities without damaging nearby structures; a minimum diameter (and possibly length) is specified; capacities verified by load tests and integrity by integrity tests.
sections.body: This work consists of constructing CFA piles per the contract plans, approved working drawings and this specification; the CFA Pile Contractor furnishes all design, materials, equipment, services, labor and supervision for design, installation and testing of the piles and pile cap connections. The contractor designs and installs the piles, selecting type, diameter, length, cap connection and installation means and methods to provide the plan load capacities without damage to nearby structures; a minimum diameter will be specified and a minimum length may be. Capacities are verified by load testing and integrity by integrity tests as required, and all piles must meet the acceptance criteria. The imperative mood is used (p. 194). Sections are cited as '(8.)1.1' so the specification can be renumbered when adapted (p. 195). (pp. 194 to 195)
key_points: The CFA Pile Contractor designs the piles, cap connections and installation means and methods (p. 194).
A minimum diameter will be specified; a minimum length may be (p. 194).
Capacity verified by load testing, integrity by integrity tests as required (p. 194).
sections.applicability: Submittal requirements for performance-based CFA pile construction contracts

sections.title: Definitions
sections.summary: Definitions: a CFA pile is formed by a hollow-stem auger with grout or concrete pumped under continuous positive pressure during withdrawal and reinforcement inserted into the fluid column; it includes conventional CFA, drilled displacement and partial displacement piles, none proprietary for bidding. Also defined: contractor, Design Engineer, Engineer, Inspector, Owner, Plans, Project Manager, Working Drawings.
sections.body: CFA pile: made by rotating a hollow-stem auger to the specified depth and injecting grout or concrete through the stem under continuous positive pressure during withdrawal, pressing upward on the soil-filled flights and laterally on the surrounding soil; reinforcement is inserted into the fluid column afterwards; includes (a) traditional CFA piles, (b) drilled displacement piles (full displacement, minimal spoil) and (c) partial displacement piles. Commentary: patented tooling does not make these 'proprietary systems' for bidding; all are similar in installation and performance. CFA Pile Contractor: firm performing the work. Design Engineer: the licensed professional engineer designing the piles, meeting (8.)1.6.2. Engineer: the Owner's representative. Inspector: the Owner's field representative. Owner: responsible agency. Plans: Owner's bidding drawings. Project Manager: contractor employee supervising the work, with at least three years on CFA projects of similar size and scope. Working Drawings: contractor drawings including detailed pile designs. (p. 195)
key_points: CFA pile: grout or concrete pumped under continuous positive pressure as the hollow-stem auger is withdrawn (p. 195).
Includes conventional CFA, drilled displacement and partial displacement piles (p. 195).
Patented tooling does not make a CFA system proprietary for bidding (p. 195).

sections.title: Reference Codes and Standards
sections.summary: Reference codes: the current AASHTO Standard Specification for Highway Bridges and the State DOT Standard Specifications, with interims; the latest edition at issue governs unless indicated; the Engineer adds others.
sections.body: The listed publications form part of the specification to the extent referenced, the latest edition at issue governing unless indicated: AASHTO Standard Specification for Highway Bridges, current edition with interims; State DOT Standard Specifications, current edition with interims. Commentary: the Engineer notes any additional publications. (p. 196)
key_points: AASHTO Standard Specification for Highway Bridges and State DOT Standard Specifications govern (p. 196).

sections.title: Available Information
sections.summary: Available information: the Owner's plan set (preliminary pile size and length, plan, profile, sections) and geotechnical report(s). Commentary: plans show design loads, minimum diameter and reinforcement, cap connection and layout, sometimes a minimum tip elevation, plus safety factors and allowable displacements; the geotechnical report belongs in the special provisions.
sections.body: Available Owner information: (1) plan sets with the preliminary pile size and length, plan view, profile and typical sections; commentary: the bidding package should give pile design loadings, minimum diameter, minimum reinforcement, pile to footing/cap connection design and layout, in some cases a minimum tip elevation, and design criteria such as minimum safety factors and maximum allowable vertical and horizontal displacements (see Chapter 6 of the circular, cited as 'Augered Cast-in-Place and Continuous Flight Auger Piles'); (2) geotechnical report(s) with borings, observation pits or other data near the piles (p. 196); commentary: subsurface conditions strongly affect the contractor's choices and bidding, so the report should be in the contract special provisions, informing bidders, reducing differing site condition claims and becoming a legal part of the contract (p. 197). (pp. 196 to 197)
key_points: Plans give design loads, minimum diameter, minimum reinforcement, cap connection and layout (p. 196).
Design criteria include minimum safety factors and allowable vertical and horizontal displacements (p. 196).
Geotechnical report included in the special provisions becomes part of the contract (p. 197).

sections.title: Project Site Survey
sections.summary: Before bidding the contractor reviews subsurface data and visits the site (geometry, access, structures); it locates and verifies utilities, reporting differences; contractor and Engineer jointly document pre-construction conditions of the site, structures and utilities.
sections.body: Before bidding the contractor reviews the subsurface information and visits the site to assess geometry, equipment access and existing structures and facilities. The contractor field-locates and verifies all utilities shown before starting and notifies the Engineer of differences that may require relocating foundation elements or modifying the design; commentary: many owners have standard utility procedures, and active and abandoned utilities can strongly affect CFA installation. Before construction the contractor and Engineer jointly inspect and document the site, existing structures and utilities. (p. 197)
key_points: Contractor visits the site and reviews subsurface data before bidding (p. 197).
Contractor field-verifies utility locations before starting work (p. 197).
Joint pre-construction condition inspection of site, structures and utilities (p. 197).

sections.title: CFA Pile Contractors Experience and Submittal of Experience
sections.summary: Commentary on contractor experience: CFA pile quality depends highly on the contractor and crew, who should show competence by documented similar projects or a defect-free demonstration pile at least the plan diameter and depth.
sections.body: Commentary: CFA pile quality is highly dependent on the skill of the contractor and the specific crew; the contractor should demonstrate competence by documenting successful similar projects or by installing a demonstration pile without defects built to at least the plan diameter and depth. (p. 197)
key_points: Competence shown by similar projects or a defect-free demonstration pile at plan diameter and depth (p. 197).
sections.applicability: Submittal requirements for performance-based CFA pile construction contracts

sections.title: Experience Requirements
sections.summary: Option of listing prequalified CFA pile contractors accepted by the Owner from prior experience submittals; a prime contractor names the intended CFA pile subcontractor a set number of days before work.
sections.body: Lists potential CFA Pile Contractors to design, furnish and install the piles, based on experience submittals previously verified and accepted by the Owner (name, address, contact, phone) (p. 197). If the work is a subcontract item, the prime contractor names the intended CFA Pile Contractor a specified number of calendar days before work for review (p. 198). (pp. 197 to 198)
key_points: Owner may list prequalified CFA pile contractors (p. 197).
Prime contractor names the CFA pile subcontractor before work (p. 198).

sections.title: Experience Requirements and Submittal
sections.summary: Required: three similar successful CFA projects in the prior two years; supervisor and rig operators with three years' CFA experience; a Project Manager (contractor employee) with three years on similar projects; a Design Engineer licensed in the state with three successful similar-capacity CFA projects in five years. Reference and personnel lists submitted; personnel changes suspend work.
sections.body: The contractor must be experienced in construction and load testing of CFA piles, documenting at least three projects in the two years before bid with CFA piles installed successfully under similar conditions; the job site supervisor needs at least three years supervising CFA installation and drill rig operators at least three years installing CFA piles. The Project Manager needs at least three years on CFA projects of similar size and scope; consultants or manufacturers' representatives may not fill the role; an employee Design Engineer may also be the Project Manager, a consultant Design Engineer may not. The Design Engineer is a Professional Engineer licensed in the state with design experience on at least three successfully completed CFA projects of similar capacity in the past five years, employee or consultant. Five copies of the project reference list (with owner contacts and load test reports) and personnel list (with experience summaries) are submitted before construction, and the Engineer approves or rejects within a set period. Work is done by the listed personnel; changes suspend work until replacements are approved, with no time extension or claims and costs on the contractor. (p. 198)
key_points: Contractor: three similar successful CFA projects in the two years before bid (p. 198).
Supervisor and drill rig operators: at least three years of CFA experience (p. 198).
Project Manager: three years on similar CFA projects; not a consultant or manufacturer's representative (p. 198).
Design Engineer: licensed in the state, three successful similar-capacity CFA projects in five years (p. 198).
Personnel changes suspend work until replacements are approved (p. 198).

sections.title: CFA Pile Design Requirements
sections.summary: Piles are designed for the plan loads by the Service Load Design (SLD) procedures of Chapters 5 and 6 of the circular, with its safety factors unless otherwise specified; design parameters and criteria come from the plans; structural design not covered there is by SLD per the current AASHTO Standard Specification for Highway Bridges (17th Edition as of 2007).
sections.body: The CFA piles are designed for the specified loadings using the Service Load Design (SLD) procedures of Chapters 5 and 6 of the circular, with geotechnical safety factors/strength factors per the circular unless otherwise specified. Soil/rock design strengths, unit weights, loads, corrosion protection, utilities, easements, rights-of-way and other criteria are as shown on the plans or specified. Structural design of any element not covered by the circular is by the SLD method per the most current AASHTO Standard Specification for Highway Bridges (17th Edition as of 2007) with interims (as printed; 6.3.1 sets structural design by LRFD). (p. 199)
key_points: Geotechnical design by Service Load Design per Chapters 5 and 6 of the circular (p. 199).
Safety factors per the circular unless otherwise specified (p. 199).
Structural design not in the circular by SLD per the AASHTO Standard Specification, 17th Edition (p. 199).

sections.title: CFA Pile Design Submittals
sections.summary: Design calculations and working drawings, signed and sealed by the approved Design Engineer, are submitted at least 60 calendar days before CFA construction; the contractor keeps overall responsibility if a consultant designs; no work until accepted, deviations resubmitted, no time or claims for incomplete submittals.
sections.body: At least 60 calendar days before planned CFA construction, submit complete design calculations and working drawings with all details, dimensions, quantities, ground profiles and sections, after verifying the structure limits and survey data. They are signed and sealed by the contractor's or the previously approved consultant Design Engineer; with a consultant, the contractor keeps overall contractual responsibility for design and construction. Set numbers of sets and sheet sizes are submitted; the Engineer approves or rejects within a set period; revisions are resubmitted; approved sets plus a Mylar sepia set are furnished. No CFA work until the submittals are acceptable; changes are resubmitted; no time adjustment or claims for incomplete submittals. (p. 199)
key_points: Design submittals at least 60 calendar days before CFA construction (p. 199).
Signed and sealed by the approved Design Engineer (p. 199).
Contractor keeps overall responsibility when a consultant designs (p. 199).
No CFA work until submittals are accepted (p. 199).

sections.title: Design Calculations
sections.summary: Design calculations include a summary report, code requirements, critical cross-sections, design criteria (strengths, unit weights, unit side and end resistances, added subsurface data), safety factors, seismic criteria, indexed calculation sheets with designer and checker initials, and notes on symbols and programs.
sections.body: Design calculations include at least: (1) a written summary report (p. 199); (2) applicable code requirements and references; (3) critical design cross-sections with strata, piezometric levels and applied loads; (4) design criteria including strengths (friction angle and cohesion), unit weights, unit skin friction and unit end-bearing values, and any added subsurface data; (5) safety factors; (6) seismic acceleration coefficient or other seismic criteria; (7) static and seismic calculation sheets with project number, location, designation, date, designer and checker initials and page numbers, with an index; (8) notes explaining symbols and computer programs. Requirements for items 2, 5 and 6 will be in the bid package if applicable (p. 200). (pp. 199 to 200)
key_points: Calculations include unit skin friction and end-bearing values and safety factors (p. 200).
Bid package may set code, safety factor and seismic requirements (p. 200).
sections.applicability: Submittal requirements for performance-based CFA pile construction contracts

sections.title: Working Drawings
sections.summary: Working drawings carry all construction and QC information: plan view (baseline, offsets, stations, locations and spacing, right-of-way, utilities, structures, drainage, explorations), elevation view, notes, curve data, quantities, typical sections with reinforcement and connections, test pile details, schedules; revised for field changes, with as-builts and revised calculations.
sections.body: Working drawings include all information for construction and quality control, unless in the contract plans: (1) plan view with reference baseline, offsets at alignment changes, beginning and end stations, pile locations and center-to-center spacing, right-of-way and easements, known utilities, adjacent structures or interferences, drainage structures or pipes (p. 200), and subsurface exploration locations; (2) elevation view with pile locations, elevations and spacing and existing and finished grades; (3) general construction notes and sequencing; (4) horizontal and vertical curve data and control points; (5) summary of quantities; (6) typical sections with spacing, diameter, reinforcement, centralizers and spacers and connections to the footing/pile cap; (7) typical details of verification and proof load test piles with reaction systems; (8) details, dimensions and schedules of piles and reinforcement. Commentary: coordinate with Owner procedures. Drawings are revised for field changes, as-builts submitted within a set period after completion, and revised calculations signed by the Design Engineer provided for all design changes (p. 201). (pp. 200 to 201)
key_points: Working drawings include all construction and quality control information (p. 200).
Include verification and proof load test pile details with reaction systems (p. 201).
As-built drawings and revised signed calculations for design changes (p. 201).

sections.title: Construction Submittals
sections.summary: Construction submittals are due at least 60 calendar days before CFA construction for review and comment; no work until acceptable; deviations resubmitted; no time or claims for incomplete submittals.
sections.body: At least 60 calendar days before planned CFA construction, submit complete construction submittals for review and comment; the Engineer comments within a set period; revisions are resubmitted; no CFA work until acceptable; changes resubmitted for approval; no adjustment in contract time or delay claims for incomplete submittals. (p. 201)
key_points: Construction submittals at least 60 calendar days before CFA construction (p. 201).
No CFA work until construction submittals are acceptable (p. 201).

sections.title: Pile Installation Plan
sections.summary: The Pile Installation Plan shows the dependability of equipment, techniques and materials, citing similar projects: equipment and calibration, procedures, sequence, target drilling and grouting parameters with ranges, reinforcement placement, mix designs, monitoring, contingencies, protection of structures. Commentary: crane rigs only for non-caving soils; at least 30,000 ft-lb torque and 5,000 lb crowd; no pile within six diameters until set.
sections.body: The plan demonstrates to the Engineer the dependability of the equipment, techniques and materials, citing similar pile sizes in similar soils with the proposed equipment, and includes at least: (1) equipment list and sizes (rigs, augers, tools, pumps, mixing and automated monitoring equipment) with calibration procedures; (2) step-by-step installation procedures; (3) installation sequence; (4) target drilling and grouting parameters with acceptable ranges (rotation speed, penetration rates, torque, crowd, grout pressures, grout volume factors); (5) reinforcement placement, support and centering; (6) mix designs with slump loss and strength development vs. time (for fly ash and/or slag); (7) and (8) monitoring and recording of drilling and of grout pressures and volumes; (9) contingency plans for equipment failure; (10) protection of adjacent structures with a monitoring plan 'as required in Section 3.1'; (11) other submittals (p. 202). Commentary: a clear plan reduces misunderstandings and claims; scrutinize rig capacity and boom lengths, torque, speed and crowd, hydraulic horsepower, and the piston-ball valve grout pump. Most U.S. CFA piling of the last 30 years used crane-mounted rigs, which cannot apply crowd and so poorly control penetration rate and soil mining; approve them only for non-caving soils after careful consideration; hydraulic rigs allow partial or full displacement piles; equipment selection is the contractor's responsibility. Stiff soils or piles over 18 in. (0.45 m) need special sizing: minimum torque 30,000 ft-lb (41 m-kN) and crowd at least 5,000 lb (22 kN), possibly insufficient. The sequence should preclude installing piles within six diameters, center to center, before the first is fully set (p. 203). (pp. 202 to 203)
key_points: Plan cites similar pile sizes and soils done with the proposed equipment (p. 202).
Target drilling and grouting parameters with acceptable ranges (p. 202).
Crane-mounted rigs cannot apply crowd; approve only for non-caving soils (p. 203).
Stiff soils or piles over 18 in. (0.45 m): minimum torque 30,000 ft-lb (41 m-kN), crowd at least 5,000 lb (22 kN) (p. 203).
No pile within six diameters, center to center, until the first is fully set (p. 203).
sections.applicability: Submittal requirements for performance-based CFA pile construction contracts

sections.title: Conformance Testing Plan
sections.summary: The Conformance Testing Plan, with the installation plan, covers pre-production static tests, production static, rapid or dynamic tests and integrity tests per (8.)3.11 and (8.)3.12; production piles use the test pile process and equipment; it lists automated monitoring equipment ((8.)3.4) and materials testing ((8.)3.2) and assigns QA/QC tasks.
sections.body: With the Pile Installation Plan the contractor submits a plan for the bid package's testing program: pre-production static load tests, production static and/or rapid and/or dynamic load tests and post-installation integrity tests in sufficient quantities to show the load and deflection criteria are met with an appropriate factor of safety; the test pile process and equipment are used for production piles (p. 203). The pre-production program sets baseline parameters; verification and integrity tests confirm acceptable piles; methods and frequencies per (8.)3.11 and (8.)3.12 and State DOT specifications. The plan lists automated measuring and recording equipment (minimums in (8.)3.4) with type, manufacturer, data, calibration records and sample records; materials sampling and testing per State DOT specifications and (8.)3.2; and states which QA/QC tasks fall to the contractor, the Inspector or both. Commentary: the program assures the Owner the piles were installed as designed and meet the load criteria (p. 204). (pp. 203 to 204)
key_points: Testing program: pre-production static tests, production static/rapid/dynamic tests, integrity tests (p. 203).
Production piles use the pre-production test pile process and equipment (p. 203).
Plan assigns QA/QC tasks to the contractor, the Inspector or both (p. 204).
sections.applicability: Submittal requirements for performance-based CFA pile construction contracts

sections.title: Pre-Construction Meeting
sections.summary: A pre-construction meeting, scheduled by the Engineer with the prime contractor, CFA pile contractor, inspectors, excavation contractor and instrumentation specialist, clarifies requirements, coordinates schedules and sets responsibilities.
sections.body: The Engineer schedules a pre-construction meeting before CFA construction, attended by the Engineer, prime contractor, CFA Pile Contractor, Inspectors, excavation contractor and Geotechnical Instrumentation Specialist (if applicable), to clarify construction requirements, coordinate the schedule and set contractual relationships and responsibilities, including excavation, anticipated subsurface conditions, installation and testing, survey control and drainage. (p. 204)
key_points: Engineer schedules a pre-construction meeting with all parties (p. 204).
sections.applicability: Submittal requirements for performance-based CFA pile construction contracts

sections.title: Materials
sections.summary: Materials conform to State DOT specifications: portland cement Types I, II, III (ASTM C150), water, aggregates, fly ash (ASTM C618 Class C or F), water reducers, fluidifier, reinforcing steel (ASTM A615), and standard flow cone, cube, slump and cylinder tests. Type III cement not used when 12 hour temperatures exceed 60 deg F; admixtures approved.
sections.body: All materials conform to the relevant State DOT Standard Specifications or as noted (p. 204): portland cement Types I, II and III (ASTM C150); water (AASHTO T 26); fine and coarse aggregate (ASTM C33 and others); fly ash (ASTM C618 Class C or F); water reducing admixtures (ASTM C494, C1017); fluidifier (ASTM C937, CRD-C 619); reinforcing steel (ASTM A615, ACI 315); grout flow cone (ASTM C939, CRD-611-94); grout cubes (ASTM C109, C942); concrete slump (ASTM C143); concrete cylinders (ASTM C31, C39). Notes: Type III cement not used when the air temperature in the 12 hours after batching will exceed 60 deg F (15 deg C); 'Type B fly ash shall not be used in conjunction with Type II Portland cement' (as printed); admixtures approved and stored per the State item; reinforcing includes assemblies. Commentary: include the State DOT's sections; a generic materials section is not possible; grout and concrete guidance is in (8.)3.2 and (8.)3.3 (p. 205). (pp. 204 to 205)
key_points: Materials conform to State DOT Standard Specifications (p. 204).
Fly ash ASTM C618 Class C or F; reinforcing steel ASTM A615 (p. 205).
Type III cement not used when air temperature in the 12 hours after batching exceeds 60 deg F (15 deg C) (p. 205).

sections.title: Construction Requirements
sections.summary: Heading for the construction requirements: site preparation, grout or concrete, auger and monitoring equipment, drilling, placement, pile head, reinforcement, cutoff, records, testing, integrity testing and unacceptable piles (8.3.1 to 8.3.13).
sections.body: Heading for the construction requirements, 8.3.1 to 8.3.13; it has no text of its own. (p. 206)
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Site Preparation and Protection of Adjacent Structures
sections.summary: Heading for site preparation (8.3.1.1) and protection of adjacent structures (8.3.1.2).
sections.body: Heading for 8.3.1.1 and 8.3.1.2; it has no text of its own. (p. 206)
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Site Preparation
sections.summary: Unsuitable material (muck, organics, soft clay) within 5 ft (1.5 m) of the surface is removed or treated before piling; deeper unsuitable material or suspected contamination is reported to the Engineer. Commentary: remove to full depth or 5 ft, whichever is less, and backfill with soil of PI 20 or less compacted to 95%.
sections.body: Muck, organics, soft clay or other unsuitable material within 5 ft (1.5 m) of the surface is removed or treated to prevent problems with pile tops, to the Engineer's satisfaction, before construction; more than 5 ft (1.5 m) of unsuitable material, or suspected hydrocarbon, refuse or hazardous contamination, is reported immediately and work proceeds as directed. Commentary: remove unsuitable material to full depth or 5 ft (1.5 m), whichever is less, and backfill with soil of plasticity index 20 or less compacted to at least 95% of maximum dry density 'as specified by ASTM D 698 (AASHTO T 180)' (as printed), within 2% of optimum moisture. (p. 206)
key_points: Remove or treat unsuitable material within 5 ft (1.5 m) of the surface before piling (p. 206).
Report more than 5 ft of unsuitable material or suspected contamination to the Engineer (p. 206).
Backfill: PI 20 or less, at least 95% of maximum dry density, within 2% of optimum (p. 206).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Protection of Adjacent Structures
sections.summary: The contractor is solely responsible for protecting adjacent structures and utilities: structures within a distance equal to the pile length are monitored to 0.01 in. (0.3 mm) by an independent party from a baseline within 10 days, with condition surveys; on any movement stop, notify and revise. Commentary: over-rotation in loose sands causes settlement; grout fracturing can heave.
sections.body: The contractor is solely responsible for evaluating, designing and monitoring measures to prevent damage to adjacent structures or utilities, including methods preventing over-excavation and grout migration, vibration control (casings, sheeting, shoring) and utility protection. Structures within a horizontal distance equal to the planned pile length are monitored for vertical and horizontal movement to 0.01 in. (0.3 mm) by an independent party approved by the Engineer, under a monitoring plan in the installation plan, beginning with a baseline no more than 10 calendar days before construction; their condition (cracks, widths) is documented before and after by inspection, photographs or video, Owner structures needing only movement monitoring unless shown (p. 206). On any movement the contractor stops, notifies the Engineer, takes immediate remedial measures, and reviews procedures, submitting a revised plan if needed. Commentary: a high rotation rate relative to penetration (over-rotation), especially in loose sands, can cause large surface settlement; grout pumping can fracture ground and travel far horizontally, lifting the surface and structures; if soil susceptible to densification is met, increase penetration rate or reduce rotation rate; condition surveys support the Engineer's evaluation (p. 207). (pp. 206 to 207)
key_points: Contractor solely responsible for protecting adjacent structures and utilities (p. 206).
Monitor structures within a distance equal to the pile length to 0.01 in. (0.3 mm) (p. 206).
Baseline no more than 10 calendar days before construction; condition documented before and after (p. 206).
On any detected movement stop, notify the Engineer and revise the installation plan as needed (p. 207).
Over-rotation in loose sands can cause large settlement; grout fracturing can lift structures (p. 207).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Grout or Concrete
sections.summary: Grout or concrete properties are judged from samples per (8.)3.2.4. Commentary: sand-cement grout is traditional and concrete now routine; keep the mix fixed once set by the test program; typically 30% and 70% of 28-day strength at 3 and 7 days; pozzolans lower permeability and extend workability but may severely retard early strength to 10 to 14 days.
sections.body: Grout or concrete properties are determined from samples taken during construction per (8.)3.2.4. Commentary: CFA piles were traditionally built with sand-cement grout; concrete is now routine and acceptable when properly specified; either is allowed, but a mix established by the test program should not be altered. Grout and concrete meeting the specification typically attain 30% and 70% of 28-day strength after 3 and 7 days. Pozzolans (fly ash, ASTM C618; 'silica flume' and slag, 'ASTM 989-94', as printed) lower permeability and retard set, extending workability, but will probably severely retard early strength gain, typically to about 10 to 14 days; mix designs include strength vs. time data (p. 207). Local DOT mixes (as for wet-method drilled shafts) may be preferred; desirable properties are fluidity, self-compaction, segregation resistance and controlled set (p. 208). (pp. 207 to 208)
key_points: Either grout or concrete allowed; do not alter a mix set by the test program (p. 207).
Typically 30% and 70% of 28-day strength after 3 and 7 days (p. 207).
Pozzolans extend workability but may severely retard early strength to about 10 to 14 days (p. 207).
Desirable: fluidity, self-compaction, segregation resistance, controlled set (p. 208).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Mix Design – Grout
sections.summary: Grout (cement, fly ash, water, sand, fluidifier, retarder): solids in suspension; flow cone per ASTM C939 or CRD 611-94 with a 3/4 in. (19 mm) outlet and an approved range (typically 10 to 25 s); shrinkage at most 0.15% (ASTM C1090); specified 28-day strength; consistency kept at least 2 hours; strength vs. time data.
sections.body: Grout of portland cement, fly ash, water, sand, fluidifier and, if needed, retarder must: (1) keep solids in suspension without excessive bleed; (2) be tested for fluid consistency by flow cone per ASTM C939 or CRD 611-94 with the outlet enlarged from 1/2 in. (12 mm) to 3/4 in. (19 mm), within an approved range of efflux time; (3) shrink no more than 0.15% vertically (ASTM C1090), cured at 100% humidity and 68 to 74 deg F (20 to 23 deg C); (4) reach the specified 28-day compressive strength; (5) include viscosity loss vs. time curves and keep the consistency range at least 2 hours or longer if the plan requires; (6) provide strength vs. time data beyond 28 days for fly ash, silica fume or slag mixes. Commentary: CFA grouts are too thick for the 1/2 in. outlet; the Corps cone's removable orifice can be taken out, while an ASTM cone must be custom made; acceptable grouts typically have efflux times of 10 to 25 seconds (p. 208); flow checks quickly indicate conformance and help identify other suspect piles if some fail later tests (p. 209). (pp. 208 to 209)
key_points: Flow cone outlet enlarged to 3/4 in. (19 mm); typical efflux 10 to 25 seconds (p. 208).
Grout shrinkage at most 0.15% vertically (ASTM C1090) (p. 208).
Keep fluid consistency at least 2 hours (p. 208).
Flow records help identify other suspect piles (p. 209).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Mix Design – Concrete
sections.summary: Concrete (cement, fly ash, water, aggregates, water reducers, retarder): solids in suspension; slump 8 +/- 1 in. (200 +/- 25 mm, ASTM C143); specified 28-day strength; slump loss and strength vs. time curves. Commentary: wet drilled shaft mixes work but CFA needs more workability; coarse aggregate typically at most 3/8 in. (9.5 mm), rounded preferred; high sand/cement content.
sections.body: Concrete of portland cement, fly ash, water, coarse and fine aggregate, water reducers and, if needed, retarder must: (1) keep solids in suspension; (2) have slump 8 in. +/- 1 in. (200 mm +/- 25 mm) (ASTM C143); (3) reach the specified 28-day strength; (4) include slump loss vs. time curves; (5) give strength vs. time data for fly ash, silica fume or slag mixes. Commentary: wet-method drilled shaft mixes are generally acceptable but CFA piles need more workability for pumping through lines and auger and for inserting reinforcement, so coarse aggregate is typically no larger than 3/8 in. (9.5 mm), rounded pea gravel being beneficial; workability comes from gradation, water-cement ratio and admixtures; angular aggregate is harder to work; sand/cement content should be high relative to coarse aggregate against segregation; fly ash may slow strength gain. (p. 209)
key_points: Concrete slump 8 in. +/- 1 in. (200 mm +/- 25 mm) (p. 209).
Coarse aggregate typically no larger than 3/8 in. (9.5 mm); rounded pea gravel beneficial (p. 209).
High sand/cement content relative to coarse aggregate resists segregation (p. 209).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Field Operations
sections.summary: Field operations: clean equipment; batch at a State approved plant, site water only with approval within the design w/cm; hold agitated up to 2.5 h at 68 deg F or less, 2 h at 68 to 100 deg F; no placement above 100 or below 39 deg F without approved procedures; screen 3/4 in. (grout) or 4 in. (concrete); positive displacement pump to at least 350 psi, volume per stroke within 3%.
sections.body: (1) Remove oil, rust inhibitors, drilling slurry and foreign material from all equipment contacting grout or concrete. (2) Batch at a State approved facility; site water only with the Engineer's prior approval and within the design water-cementitious ratio. (3) Continuously agitated material may be held up to 2.5 hours at air temperature not above 68 deg F (20 deg C), or 2 hours between 68 and 100 deg F (20 and 38 deg C) if other than Type III cement; no placement above 100 deg F (38 deg C) or below 39 deg F (4 deg C) without approved hot or cold weather procedures; retarded mixes per their design. (4) A screen with openings no larger than 3/4 in. (19 mm) for grout or 4 in. (100 mm) for concrete between truck and pump. (5) A positive displacement pump of known volume per stroke able to develop at least 350 psi (2,400 kPa) at the pump, sized for smooth delivery and small pressure drops; the stroke volume demonstrated within 3% and recalibrated when performance is suspect. (6) Automatic measurements per (8.)3.4 and records per (8.)3.10. (7) The minimum grout pressure at the pump outlet or auger top in the approved drawings or plan is maintained throughout. (p. 210)
key_points: Site water only with the Engineer's approval, within the design water-cementitious ratio (p. 210).
Hold agitated up to 2.5 h at 68 deg F (20 deg C) or less, 2 h from 68 to 100 deg F (p. 210).
No placement above 100 deg F (38 deg C) or below 39 deg F (4 deg C) without approved procedures (p. 210).
Screen openings no larger than 3/4 in. (19 mm) for grout, 4 in. (100 mm) for concrete (p. 210).
Positive displacement pump to at least 350 psi (2,400 kPa); stroke volume within 3% (p. 210).
Maintain the approved minimum grout pressure at the pump outlet or auger top (p. 210).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Grout or Concrete Sampling and Testing
sections.summary: Strength samples from truck discharge: 6 x 12 in. cylinders or 2 in. cubes (10% higher requirement); at least six per 50 yd3 (38 m3), per working day and per mix; two tested at 7 days, two at 28 days, two in reserve. Every truck tested for flow cone (or slump) and temperature before the hopper. Smaller grout cylinders only with approval.
sections.body: Strength samples are taken from the truck discharge before pumping: concrete cylinders 6 in. (150 mm) by 12 in. (300 mm), or sized for aggregate per ASTM C39; grout 2 in. (50 mm) cubes with a 10% higher required strength than cylinders. At least six samples per 50 yd3 (38 m3), at least six per working day and per mix, cured and tested per State DOT specifications; at minimum two tested at 7 days, two at 28 days (meeting (8.)3.2.1 or (8.)3.2.2) and two in reserve. Every truck is sampled for flow cone (grout) or slump (concrete) and temperature before discharge into the pump hopper; the Engineer may require more. Commentary: smaller grout cylinders (3 x 6 in. or 2 x 4 in.) only with prior approval and a correlation to the mix design method; frequencies are minimums the Engineer may raise, or relax for non-critical foundations; State testing manuals may be referenced. (p. 211)
key_points: Grout cubes 2 in. (50 mm) with a 10% higher strength requirement than cylinders (p. 211).
At least six samples per 50 yd3 (38 m3), per working day and per mix (p. 211).
Two samples tested at 7 days, two at 28 days, two held in reserve (p. 211).
Every truck tested for flow cone or slump and temperature before the pump hopper (p. 211).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Auger Equipment
sections.summary: Augers: continuous flights (joint gaps at most 1 in.), length for 20% more than plan depth, outside diameter at least 97% of design, single helix, clean stem, leads marked every 1 ft; flat-bottom cutting head and sealed injection port; ground guide plus a mid-height guide over 40 ft (12 m) unless a hydraulic fixed mast with a stem of 10 in. or more.
sections.body: Flights are continuous from top to cutting face, gaps only at joints and at most 1 in. (25 mm); augers on site can reach 20% beyond the approved pile depth; flighting is uniform and the outside diameter at least 97% of the design diameter; single helix only; the hollow stem is kept clean; leads are marked every 1 ft (0.3 m), visible from the ground. Commentary: these are minimums; alternatives via the installation plan; full or partial displacement tools should also be considered. The bottom flights and teeth form as flat a pile base as feasible; the injection port is sealed against water and soil during drilling. A guide at the ground surface on the leads, plus one at about half the auger length above it if the auger exceeds 40 ft (12 m), not required on hydraulic fixed-mast platforms with a stem of 10 in. (250 mm) or more; leads restrained against rotation. The rig must penetrate without drawing soil laterally into the bore 'as is described in Section 3.5' and reach at least 20% beyond the approved depth. (p. 212)
key_points: Gaps in flighting only at joints and at most 1 in. (25 mm) (p. 212).
Augers and rigs able to reach 20% beyond the approved pile depth (p. 212).
Auger outside diameter at least 97% of the design diameter; single helix only (p. 212).
Leads marked every 1 ft (0.3 m) (p. 212).
Intermediate guide for augers over 40 ft (12 m), except hydraulic fixed masts with stems of 10 in. (250 mm) or more (p. 212).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Automatic Measurement and Recording Equipment
sections.summary: Automatic measurements in drilling (rotation, injection point depth, torque, crowd) and grouting (volume, maximum and minimum pressure, rotation, injection depth), all against injection point depth, with position and rotation indicators, load cells, flowmeters and transducers; calibrated within 3% at project start and when performance is suspect.
sections.body: Minimum automatic drilling measurements: auger rotation, depth of the injection point, torque and crowd force (p. 212), referenced to injection point depth via a rotational position indicator on the auger head, an electronic position indicator on the crane line or boom, and torque and thrust load cells on the auger head. Minimum grouting measurements: volume, maximum and minimum pressure, rotation if rotated and injection depth, via electronic flowmeters and pressure transducers in the line and the position and rotation indicators. All equipment is calibrated at project start to within 3% per the manufacturer and recalibrated when the Engineer suspects performance has changed. Commentary: real-time evaluation of each pile; abnormal records can trigger integrity or verification tests (p. 213). (pp. 212 to 213)
key_points: Drilling: rotation, injection point depth, torque and crowd (p. 212).
Grouting: volume, maximum and minimum pressure, rotation and injection depth (p. 213).
Electronic flowmeters and pressure transducers in the grout line (p. 213).
Calibrated to within 3% at project start and when performance is suspect (p. 213).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Drilling
sections.summary: Drill only with enough grout or concrete on site; parameters within the plan's verified ranges, as for test piles; center within 3 in. (75 mm), plumb or batter within 2%; no pile within six diameters until the first is set; no open borehole; continuous penetration without excess spoil. Commentary: 1.5 to 2 revolutions per pitch in cohesionless, 2 to 3 in cohesive soils; refusal under 1 ft/min.
sections.body: Drilling reaches the approved design dimensions through whatever is encountered, starting only with enough grout or concrete on site to finish the pile; drilling parameters stay within the plan's ranges verified by pre-production testing, using the test piles' procedures. Pile centers within 3 in. (75 mm) of plan location; plumb within 2% or within 2% of design batter (p. 213); violations may be rejected or replaced at the contractor's expense. Piles within six diameters, center to center, wait until the first pile is shown fully set. The auger is never extracted so as to leave an open borehole or let water in; if raised and re-inserted, the pile is deepened or other measures taken. The auger advances continuously at a rotation rate preventing excess spoil, the rate set in the test program and verified by monitoring. Termination and refusal criteria come from the pre-production program; at early refusal stop rotation and evaluate with the Engineer; obstructions go to the Engineer and Design Engineer. Commentary: advance at least one pitch per 1.5 to 2 revolutions in cohesionless soils or 2 to 3 in cohesive soils, loose sands needing the stricter guideline; refusal is generally under 1 ft/minute (0.3 m/minute) with suitable equipment, an indicator of a strong layer but not the sole basis for conventional CFA tip levels, though usable for DD piles if verified by load tests (p. 214). (pp. 213 to 214)
key_points: Start drilling only with enough grout or concrete on site to complete the pile (p. 213).
Center within 3 in. (75 mm); plumb or batter within 2% (p. 213).
No pile within six diameters, center to center, until the first is fully set (p. 214).
Never leave an open unsupported borehole; re-inserting the auger requires added depth or measures (p. 214).
Advance one pitch per 1.5 to 2 revolutions in cohesionless and 2 to 3 in cohesive soils (p. 214).
Refusal generally under 1 ft/minute (0.3 m/minute); not the sole tip criterion for conventional CFA piles (p. 214).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Placement of Grout or Concrete
sections.summary: Grouting starts within 5 minutes of reaching depth: lift 6 to 12 in. to blow the plug, re-insert to depth, then withdraw smoothly while pumping (positive rotation only) keeping positive tip pressure; volume recorded every 2 ft; inadequate volume over 5 ft (1.5 m) is a basis for rejection; volume factor within 7.5% of target (typical 1.15 to 1.2, over 1.5 suggests mining); suspended placement means re-drilling.
sections.body: Placement begins within 5 minutes of reaching planned depth, pumping with enough pressure (at the auger top) to form the pile and fill soft or porous zones. The plug or cover plate is removed by pressure or a central bar, lifting the auger only 6 to 12 in. (0.15 to 0.3 m), minimizing water inflow and soil movement, then re-inserting the tip to at least the original depth. Supply rate during withdrawal ensures a continuous monolithic shaft of at least full section, free of soil inclusions and segregation; the auger is extracted smoothly while pumping, any rotation positive. Coordination is shown by positive tip pressure and a small volume oversupply, verified by automated monitoring; volume vs. depth recorded at intervals of 2 ft (0.6 m) or less; the minimum oversupply is set in pre-production and maintained; inadequate volume over a 5 ft (1.5 m) interval is a basis for rejection. Commentary: typical grout volume factors 1.15 to 1.2, 1.15 a minimum; over 1.5 suggests soil mining, though sometimes acceptable if tests confirm (p. 215). The factor must be within 7.5% of the target, else the pile is unacceptable ((8.)3.13). If placement is suspended, the pile is re-drilled, in place if still fluid, otherwise in a new location with revised plan and drawings. Commentary: pull with no rotation (a static base) or slow drilling-direction rotation (avoids sticking, spreads off-center discharge), never fast enough to lift soil; a short-volume pile may be re-drilled, acceptance being the Engineer's call (p. 216). (pp. 215 to 216)
key_points: Start grouting within 5 minutes after reaching planned depth (p. 215).
Lift the auger only 6 to 12 in. (0.15 to 0.3 m) to release the plug, then re-insert to depth (p. 215).
Any rotation during extraction must be positive (drilling direction) (p. 215).
Record volume vs. depth at intervals of 2 ft (0.6 m) or less (p. 215).
Inadequate volume over a 5 ft (1.5 m) interval is a basis for rejection (p. 215).
Typical grout volume factor 1.15 to 1.2; 1.15 minimum; over 1.5 suggests soil mining (p. 215).
Volume factor within 7.5% of the target, else unacceptable (p. 216).
Suspended placement: re-drill in place if fluid, else in a new location (p. 216).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Pile Head Finishing and Protection
sections.summary: Right after placement remove excess grout and spoil, set a temporary device extending at least 1 ft (0.3 m) above and below grade, remove fallen soil before initial set, and remove the device after set without disturbing the soil.
sections.body: Immediately after placing fluid grout or concrete the contractor removes excess material and spoil near the top and sets a temporary device in the top of the excavation extending at least 1 ft (0.3 m) above and below grade to keep spoil out; then removes any loose soil in the column with the approved tools before initial set; the device is removed after set without disturbing the surrounding soil. (p. 216)
key_points: Temporary device at least 1 ft (0.3 m) above and below grade at the pile top (p. 216).
Remove fallen soil from the column before initial set (p. 216).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Reinforcing Steel Placement
sections.summary: Reinforcement is lowered into the fluid column, clean, centered with plastic or cementitious spacers (no metal), cages assembled as units, spirals tied at 1 ft or less, splices only where shown, no welding unless weldable; placed immediately by gravity or hand push, never vibrated or driven; held until initial set or 24 hours. Commentary: in dry or moist sand place within 10 minutes.
sections.body: Reinforcement is lowered into the fluid column, free of oil, soil, excessive rust or deleterious material (p. 216), centered by plastic or cementitious spacers along and around it; metallic spacers are not permitted; centralizers are approved by the Engineer. Cages are assembled and placed as a unit, spirals tied to the bars at no more than 1 ft (0.3 m); welding only of specified weldable steel. No splices except where shown and no permanently distorted bars; a pile lengthened after cages are made is extended by splicing near the cage bottom, not by welding unless weldable. Steel is placed immediately after screening the grout and before set, by gravity or gentle hand push, never vibrated, driven or mechanically guided, and held at the surface until initial set or 24 hours, whichever is longer. Commentary: in considerable dry or moist sand the cage should go in as soon as possible, under 10 minutes if possible; steel spacers may greatly accelerate corrosion, but steel centering guides such as a wire 'basket' or 'football' at the base of single-rod reinforcement may be used (as printed); retarded mixes may need over 24 hours to initial set; the plan states support duration (p. 217). (pp. 216 to 217)
key_points: Plastic or cementitious spacers only; metallic spacers not permitted (p. 217).
Spiral tied to longitudinal bars at no more than 1 ft (0.3 m) (p. 217).
Reinforcement never vibrated, driven or mechanically guided into position (p. 217).
Support reinforcement until initial set or 24 hours, whichever is longer (p. 217).
In dry or moist sand place the cage within about 10 minutes if possible (p. 217).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Pile Cut-Off
sections.summary: Pile tops are cut off square at the approved elevations by removing fresh or cutting hardened grout after initial set; the finished top must be within 1 in. (25 mm) below or 3 in. (75 mm) above the approved elevation.
sections.body: The contractor cuts off pile tops square with the axis at the approved elevations, by removing fresh grout or concrete or cutting hardened material down to cutoff any time after initial set; the finished top is no more than 1 in. (25 mm) below or 3 in. (75 mm) above the approved elevation. (p. 217)
key_points: Finished pile top within 1 in. (25 mm) below or 3 in. (75 mm) above the approved elevation (p. 217).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Inspection and Records
sections.summary: Contractor and Engineer keep records for each pile: 21 items including location, elevations, toe depth, length, auger diameter, reinforcement, flow cone or slump and volumes, theoretical volume, times, weather, samples, and automated readings every 2 ft (0.6 m) or less of rotation, volume and pump pressures, plus torque and crowd if specified; data within 24 hours.
sections.body: The contractor keeps accurate records of each pile (the Engineer similar ones): location; ground elevation; toe depth and elevation; top of grout or concrete; length; auger diameter; reinforcement details; flow cone efflux time and grout volume or slump and concrete volume; theoretical hole volume (auger diameter); reinforcement depth; dates and times of drilling, mixing, truck arrival (with batch tickets), pumping and reinforcement placement; weather and air temperature; sample identification; other pertinent data; and automated readings at minimum of rotation vs. depth and volume vs. outlet depth per 2 ft (0.6 m) or less, average maximum and minimum pump stroke pressures at ground level and, if directed, near the auger head, and, if specified, torque and crowd (p. 218). Data are provided to the Engineer within 24 hours of completing the pile, in numerical or graphical form (p. 219). (pp. 218 to 219)
key_points: Records cover volumes vs. depth, flow cone or slump, times, weather and samples (p. 218).
Automated readings every 2 ft (0.6 m) or less (pp. 218 to 219).
Data to the Engineer within 24 hours of completing each pile (p. 219).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Testing
sections.summary: Testing follows State DOT specifications or deep foundation load test specifications. Commentary: scope depends on loads and pile numbers; non-critical structures (sound walls, signs, light poles) may need less testing, even no load test for a qualified contractor's lightly loaded piles.
sections.body: Testing conforms to the State DOT Standard Specifications, or to deep foundation load test specifications if CFA piles are not addressed. Commentary: Chapter 7 discusses testing; scope depends on loads and number of piles; for 'non-critical structures' such as sound barrier walls, overhead signs and light or signal poles the Engineer may require less frequent testing, and a qualified contractor with consistent technique may not need a load test for a lightly loaded pile, monitoring records and integrity tests giving enough confidence. (p. 219)
key_points: Testing per State DOT specifications or deep foundation load test specifications (p. 219).
Non-critical structures may need less testing; a lightly loaded pile may need no load test (p. 219).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Pre-Production Testing
sections.summary: Pre-production test piles (and reaction piles) meet all production requirements and set target penetration rate, pressure/volume relations (grout factor +/-7.5% for production), torque and crowd for displacement piles, mix parameters, and design correlations, possibly revising the design; production piles use them. Commentary: large projects add calibrated rapid or dynamic tests.
sections.body: Pre-production test piles (including reaction piles) meet all construction, monitoring and inspection requirements of production piles; results establish target penetration rates, pressure/volume relations (the test piles' grout factor +/-7.5% used for production), target torque and crowd for displacement or partial displacement piles, mix parameters such as grout flow and admixtures (p. 219), and design correlations of side and base resistance, possibly revising the design with approval; all are used for production piles. Commentary: unlike past load-test-only programs, test piles establish installation criteria as well as capacity so production piles match a test pile; one or more static tests, on very large projects one static test plus calibrated rapid or dynamic tests; testing concurrent with production start saves mobilization on small to medium projects but limits design changes (p. 220). (pp. 219 to 220)
key_points: Test piles meet all production construction, monitoring and inspection requirements (p. 219).
Production grout factor: the test piles' value +/-7.5% (p. 219).
Pre-production tests may lead to design revision with the Engineer's approval (p. 220).
The production pile should be the same as a test pile (p. 220).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Verification Load Testing
sections.summary: Verification tests on at least 2% of production piles (more if required) by static, rapid or dynamic tests per State DOT specifications. Commentary: periodic tests confirm continued adequate capacity; rapid (Statnamic, Fundex) or dynamic (drop hammer) tests are efficient, calibrated to static tests in pre-production.
sections.body: Verification tests on at least 2% of production piles, and more as required, show production piles meet the load-deflection criteria, by static, rapid (RLT) or dynamic (DLT) tests or combinations, RLT and DLT per State DOT specifications or approval. Commentary: one pre-production test shows only that pile's performance; periodic verification tests confirm techniques keep giving adequate capacity; RLT (Statnamic, Fundex) or DLT (drop hammer) can test many piles efficiently; calibrating them to static tests in pre-production reduces delays. (p. 220)
key_points: Verification tests on at least 2% of production piles (p. 220).
Static, rapid (RLT) or dynamic (DLT) tests or combinations (p. 220).
Calibrate RLT or DLT to static tests during pre-production (p. 220).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Integrity Testing
sections.summary: Integrity tests on at least 20% of production piles (sonic echo, impulse response, crosshole sonic, gamma) by an independent consultant; access tubes fixed to the cage and capped. Commentary: tubes about one per 1 ft of cage diameter, Schedule 40 steel for crosshole (PVC only within 72 hours), PVC for gamma; e.g., test the first 10 to 15 piles, then adjust.
sections.body: Post-installation integrity tests on at least 20% of production piles: sonic echo, impulse response, crosshole sonic, backscatter gamma and others, per the bid documents and State DOT specifications. Access tubes acceptable to the testing firm are secured to the reinforcement and capped before insertion, the piles shown on the drawings and test program. An independent consultant acceptable to the Engineer performs and interprets the tests. Commentary: down-tube tests (crosshole sonic, single-hole sonic 'SST', gamma, fiber-optic camera) are most reliable and need tubes and expert interpretation; the Engineer decides acceptance from records, the expert's report and analysis of the possible effect; tubes for sonic or gamma testing are spaced evenly at about one per 1 ft (0.3 m) of cage diameter; crosshole tubes Schedule 40 steel (PVC debonds after a few days), PVC only for gamma unless crosshole tests are within 72 hours (p. 221); more than 20% where experience is limited or problems are expected; a typical approach tests the first 10 to 15 piles then keeps 20%, reduces or perhaps eliminates testing if records match (p. 222). (pp. 221 to 222)
key_points: Integrity tests on at least 20% of production piles (p. 221).
An independent consultant performs and interprets integrity tests (p. 221).
Access tubes about one per 1 ft (0.3 m) of cage diameter (p. 221).
Crosshole tubes Schedule 40 steel; PVC only for gamma unless crosshole tests within 72 hours (p. 221).
Test the first 10 to 15 piles, then keep, reduce or perhaps eliminate testing (pp. 221 to 222).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Unacceptable Piles
sections.summary: Unacceptable piles fail the load and deflection criteria; rejection bases: failed integrity or verification tests, records showing inadequate penetration, volume or pressure, out-of-tolerance position, plumbness or top elevation, low strength or grout factor, reinforcement not as designed, visible contamination or honeycombing. They are replaced or repaired at the contractor's expense.
sections.body: Unacceptable piles do not meet the load and deflection criteria; bases for rejection: (1) integrity tests judged unacceptable; (2) a verification test not meeting the design load and deflection criteria with an appropriate factor of safety; (3) monitoring or inspection records showing inadequate penetration rates, volume factors, pressures or other parameters outside the pre-production criteria; (4) position, plumbness or batter outside (8.)3.5; (5) top elevation outside (8.)3.9; (6) strength or grout factor below design; (7) reinforcement not as designed; (8) visible contamination, excessive grout settlement, structural damage or honeycombing. They are replaced or repaired at the contractor's expense as directed. Commentary: lateral communication between piles or excessive grout takes may also make a pile unacceptable; options include abandoning the pile, switching to concrete, or grouting as well as possible and re-drilling after initial set, with the Engineer's and Design Engineer's judgment. (p. 222)
key_points: Eight listed bases for rejection, including records outside pre-production criteria (p. 222).
Grout strength or grout factor below design is a basis for rejection (p. 222).
Unacceptable piles replaced or repaired at the contractor's expense (p. 222).
Lateral communication between piles or excessive grout takes may also make a pile unacceptable (p. 222).
sections.applicability: Performance-based construction requirements for CFA pile installation in transportation projects

sections.title: Measurement
sections.summary: Measurement: CFA piles per pile, pre-production testing as a lump sum, integrity and verification load tests per pile.
sections.body: CFA pile foundations are measured per pile; pre-production testing as a lump sum; integrity tests and verification load tests per pile. (p. 223)
key_points: Piles measured per pile; pre-production testing lump sum (p. 223).
sections.applicability: Guide specification provisions for CFA pile construction contracts

sections.title: Payment
sections.summary: Payment at unit prices per accepted pile, per pile with access tubes, per integrity, rapid or dynamic test, and a lump sum for pre-production testing; unit prices apply to extensions up to 120% of the drawing depth, beyond which, or for other diameters, prices are renegotiated.
sections.body: Work measured under (8.)4 is paid at bid unit prices: (1) per accepted pile; (2) per pile with access tubes for down-hole integrity testing; (3) per integrity test, (4) per rapid load test and (5) per dynamic load test on a production pile; (6) lump sum for the pre-production test program. Quantities are those on the approved drawings as accepted unless changed in writing. Unit prices apply to extensions up to 120% of the drawing depth when required by the Engineer, length measured from top of grout to pile bottom; deeper extensions or other diameters are renegotiated. (p. 223)
key_points: Unit prices apply to pile extensions up to 120% of the drawing depth (p. 223).
Beyond 120% depth or for other diameters, unit prices are renegotiated (p. 223).
sections.applicability: Guide specification provisions for CFA pile construction contracts
